rv.q: The show's creators have fashioned a chronological journey through Lennon's life that feels more like a museum exhibit than a theatrical experience.
But diminishing the wit and intelligence of “the smart Beatle” is close to criminal.
It says everything about the vapid "Lennon" that your instinctive response to this complex apparition is, "Who is that man anyway, and what is he doing here?"
A fierce primal scream is surely the healthiest response to the agony of 'Lennon,' the jerry-built musical shrine.
Should you plop down $100 for a theater ticket or just stay home and listen to your old records? In the case of 'Lennon,' the answer is easy: Light one up and put on the stereo.
Lennon is the most criminally boring jukebox 'musical' to open to date, utterly sanitizing and whitewashing its subject's life so as to remove from him any and all controversy and rebellious fire.
Despite their heroic efforts, Menken and the rest of his creative team never shake the feeling of familiarity and predictability that plagues every scene.

cn.t: Critics savage this jukebox musical as a lifeless, jerry-built shrine to Lennon that feels more like a museum exhibit than theater. The consensus: skip the show and just listen to the records at home.
